newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta okays Shell Canada plant expansion.
newsitem.headline: Alberta okays Shell Canada plant expansion.

text.p: Alberta's Energy and Utilities Board said on Wednesday it approved Shell Canada Ltd's application to increase the amount of sour gas processed at its Caroline, Alberta natural gas plant.
Shell Canada, which built the plant in the early part of the decade, applied in February 1996 to increase the hydrogen sulphide-laden gas throughput at the facility by 15 percent.
The AEUB made its decision after a public hearing in October held in Caroline, about 100 km northwest of Calgary.
The Caroline plant currently is capable of processing 2.8 million cubic metres of natural gas, 7,200 cubic metres of gas liquids and 4,000 tonnes of sulphur per day.

Alberta's energy regulator said the approval carried a number of conditions, including Shell Canada conducting a thorough review of potential increases in "fugitive" emissions and setting up a formal program to respond to public complaints.
